content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp are crustaceans from the Penaeidae family. In this product they are peeled, coated in a breadcrumb mixture and then baked or broiled. They have a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp outer crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp can grow up to 30 cm, but most market varieties are small (5–10 cm).
Coating is often made from wheat flour, breadcrumbs and spices, though gluten‑free versions exist.
Baking retains more nutrients than deep‑frying.
Shrimp are one of the fastest‑growing seafood species; they can be farmed in 3–4 months.
In some cultures shrimp are served cold, uncoated, as a “cocktail” with dipping sauce.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide about 20 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g serving.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When baked, coated shrimp contain little fat, with most calories coming from protein.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium supports immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Shrimp supply zinc, iron and phosphorus, important for metabolism.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Coating and trans fats
items.content: If the coating is made with partially hydrogenated oils, it may contain trans fats.

items.title: Microbial contamination
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth and foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a main dish, slice into salads, add to pasta or rice. They are easy to eat with fingers, but can also be cut into bite‑size pieces. Pair with lemon, garlic, herbs or a light yogurt‑based sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen coated shrimp at –18 °C. After thawing, store in the refrigerator for no more than 2 days and cook promptly. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
